feedback: Written before this robot races. Evidence from earlier races: iterations 0 to 6 all ended off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m on every track. Span ±0.05 m removed line loss (iteration 1). The 16 mm footprint kept line loss at zero but left max_error unchanged (iteration 2). Iteration 4 tested wheel_track 0.15 m with kp scaled to 4.4 and gave the same max_error (0.0614, 0.0611, 0.0609) with higher control effort. That result is the closest evidence to your narrower-track test, and it argues that track width does not set the excursion. I expect the same here, so I do not predict a score. Your claim that a narrower track gives more turning authority is physically right (more yaw per PWM difference), and I have matched gain with kp 2.9 so the test isolates track width. I also have no per-step telemetry, so I cannot say whether the excursion happens at the start of the run or at a particular bend. Please do not treat the start-up question as settled. Next step depends on the race. If max_error stays near 0.061 m with line loss at zero, stop testing wheel_track, hold the iteration-2 row, and propose a different hypothesis. If line loss returns on the narrow track, revert to 0.12 m rather than widening the span, since the wider span is untested at ±0.07 m and the evidence favours the current row.
requested_changes: Keep the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m and y = 0.04 m, and test wheel_track 0.10 m as the single geometry change. Report max_error and line_loss_events per track.

If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, return to wheel_track 0.12 m and propose a hypothesis other than track width, since width has now been tested at 0.10 m and 0.15 m without moving the excursion.

If line loss returns at 0.10 m, revert to 0.12 m rather than widening the span to ±0.07 m, because the span change was only tested at ±0.05 m and the iteration-2 row has zero line loss on oval and slalom.
